purpose: Observe the native D3D11 lower swap returned beneath the verified ReShade 6.8 factory wrapper before ReShade constructs its own swap wrapper.

target.signature_observed: Valid Microsoft Windows Authenticode signature on 2026-09-29

original.validation: The live ReShade 6.8 wrapper must match its own pinned hash/table/method, [wrapper+8] must name an executable downstream factory, its table and slot-10 method must share the loaded System32/dxgi.dll owner, and the full file hash/size, mapped image size, table RVA, slot pointer and 16-byte method prologue must match. An existing different slot owner is not replaced.

replacement.representation: Atomic pointer-slot compare/exchange to a process-lifetime RazKolbas pass-through callback; no instruction bytes or on-disk file are changed.

abi.behavior: Call the exact prior native method once and return its unchanged HRESULT/output; inspect the returned lower swap read-only for the selected factory only. FG remains Off and no swap pointer is substituted.

lifetime.installation: Inside the verified ReShade factory callback before it calls its native delegate; a process-lifetime lease holds the expected method and selected factory identity.
lifetime.ownership: The callback DLL and native module are pinned; the pointer write is atomic and the previous method is called directly, avoiding recursion.
lifetime.removal: No hot removal while callbacks may execute; uninstall requires process exit.

recovery.disable: Add win11-dxgi.factory.create-native-lower-v1 to Patching.DisabledPatchIds and restart Skyrim.
recovery.failure_scope: Identity, path, prologue, ownership or compare/exchange rejection leaves the native method unchanged and calls through the existing ReShade factory route.

evidence: User-started 0.1.127 V5.4 game log: ReShade wrapper [this+8] was 0x1933ccfae10, native factory table 0x7ffc0b5f1428 and slot-10 method 0x7ffc0b5b7c90; the method page was executable and its owner was dxgi.dll.
A separate local x64 process loaded Microsoft-signed System32/dxgi.dll at 0x7ffc0b550000 and independently read that exact absolute table and method pointer, yielding RVAs 0xa1428 and 0x67c90.
A WARP integration test atomically replaced this exact native vtable slot in its own process, forwarded CreateSwapChain to the original method once, observed a real swap, and restored the slot.
